context: 'Ce pull' = this sweater. Point and ask. More formal: 'Combien coûte ce pull ?'
'Coûter' = to cost. Liaison: neuf euros [nuh-vuh-ROH].

front: C'est un peu trop cher pour moi.
pronunciation: [seh tan puh troh SHEHR poor MWAH]
back: It's a bit too expensive for me.
context: A polite way to say no to a price.

front: Vous avez quelque chose de moins cher ?
pronunciation: [voo zah-vay kel-kuh shohz duh mwan SHEHR]
context: 'Quelque chose de' + adjective: quelque chose de plus grand, de moins cher.
'Essayer' = to try (on). 'La cabine d'essayage' = the fitting room.
Often limited to a few items: 'trois articles maximum'.
'La taille' = clothing size (also height and waist). For shoes: 'la pointure'.
'Faire du' + size. European sizes: a women's 38 is roughly a US 8.

back: Do you have it in a bigger size?
context: Also: en plus petit, en bleu, en noir.

front: Il est trop petit, il me serre.
pronunciation: [eel eh troh puh-TEE, eel muh SEHR]
context: 'Serrer' = to be tight. 'C'est trop large' = it's too loose.
'Aller à quelqu'un' = to suit someone. Sales assistants say it a lot!
The answer to 'Je peux vous aider ?' when you don't need help.
'Le' replaces the item (le pull). For a feminine item: 'Je la prends.'

back: How would you like to pay?
context: The cashier's question. 'Par carte' (by card), 'en espèces' (in cash).
Small shops sometimes require a minimum: 'à partir de 10 euros'.
'La monnaie' = change or coins. Not 'money', which is 'l'argent'.

front: Je peux avoir un sac, s'il vous plaît ?
pronunciation: [zhuh puh ah-vwahr an SAK, seel voo PLEH]
back: Can I have a bag, please?
context: Plastic bags are banned in French shops; paper or reusable bags often cost a little.
'Les soldes' are the official sales periods in France, in January and in summer.

front: Il y a moins vingt pour cent sur tous les manteaux.
pronunciation: [eel yah mwan van poor SAHN sür too lay mahn-TOH]
back: There's twenty percent off all coats.
context: 'Moins 20 %' = 20% off. 'Le manteau' (coat) has the plural 'manteaux'.

back: I'd like to exchange this shirt.
context: 'Échanger' = to exchange; 'se faire rembourser' = to get a refund. Keep 'le ticket de caisse' (receipt).

front: Vous avez le ticket de caisse ?
context: 'La caisse' = the checkout/till; 'le caissier, la caissière' = cashier.

front: un pantalon / un jean / une jupe
context: 'Un pantalon' is singular in French (one pair of trousers).

front: une chemise / un tee-shirt / une veste
context: 'Une veste' = jacket; 'un gilet' = cardigan or vest.

front: des chaussures / des baskets / des bottes
context: 'Les baskets' (sneakers) is everyday French; 'les tennis' is also heard.

front: un manteau / une écharpe / un bonnet
context: Winter essentials. 'Des gants' = gloves.

front: Je cherche un cadeau pour ma mère.
pronunciation: [zhuh shersh an kah-DOH poor mah MEHR]
back: I'm looking for a present for my mother.
context: 'Vous pouvez me faire un paquet cadeau ?' = Can you gift-wrap it?

front: Le marché a lieu tous les mardis matin.
pronunciation: [luh mar-SHAY ah lyuh too lay mar-dee mah-TAN]
back: The market is held every Tuesday morning.
context: 'Avoir lieu' = to take place. Open-air markets are a central part of French life.

front: Un kilo de tomates, s'il vous plaît.
pronunciation: [an kee-loh duh toh-MAHT, seel voo PLEH]
context: At the market, the seller usually picks the produce for you: don't touch!
What every French shopkeeper asks. Answer: 'Ce sera tout, merci.'
Also: 'C'est tout.' Then: 'Ça fait combien ?'

front: la boulangerie, la boucherie, la pharmacie
context: Many shop names end in -erie: la fromagerie, la poissonnerie, la librairie (bookshop!).

front: La librairie est à côté de la poste.
pronunciation: [lah lee-breh-REE eh tah koh-TAY duh lah POST]
back: The bookshop is next to the post office.
context: False friend: 'une librairie' sells books; a library is 'une bibliothèque'.

front: Le magasin ferme à dix-neuf heures.
context: Many small shops close for lunch and on Sundays.
Literally 'window-licking'! A fun everyday expression.

front: Je n'ai pas assez d'argent sur moi.
pronunciation: [zhuh neh pah zah-SAY dar-ZHAHN sür MWAH]
back: I don't have enough money on me.
context: 'Assez de' = enough. 'L'argent' = money (also silver).
